title: Empirical safety harness for autonomous commit of Optimize recommendations
creator: Maya Thompson
description: Build a data-driven safety harness that allows Optimize to automatically commit batching and caching recommendations with measurable guardrails. The harness must run lightweight statistical checks during a shadow/candidate window, enable fast automated rollback on regressions, and integrate human approval hooks for high-risk changes.
motivation: Current Optimize suggestions require manual triage for many customers. We want a reliable, explainable, and reversible autopilot path that reduces operator effort while keeping customer SLAs safe and auditable.
acceptance_criteria: Can run candidate recommendations in shadow mode against live traffic for a configurable window without affecting production outputs
Automated statistical checks detect both cost regressions (>10% token cost increase) and quality regressions (decrease in pass-rate on customer-defined evals) with configurable thresholds
Automatic rollback trigger executes within 60s of breach and reverts the config with annotated audit event
Console shows a clear phased-status (shadow -> canary -> committed) with timeline and decision rationale
Human approval step available for any recommendation touching private models, customer-locked policies, or exceeding user-defined risk score
implementation_plan: Design: define shadow mode semantics, candidate scoring, and rollback hooks (owner: Diego)
Runtime: extend router to support dual-write + shadow-metrics emission for candidate configs (owner: runtime team)
Validator: implement lightweight online stats engine (CUSUM and A/A baselining) and quality check integration with eval service
Control plane: orchestration for staged promotion (shadow -> canary -> commit) and API for manual approvals
Console UX: add timeline card, risk score breakdown, and one-click rollback button
E2E: integration tests + chaos experiments to validate rollback path under high traffic
test_plan: Offline replay: run candidate configs on historical traces and compare token cost and latency distributions
Shadow-run: 100% shadow for 48h on subset of customers with monitoring only
Canary-run: 5% traffic burst with automated gating for 24h
Regression simulation: inject latency/cost anomalies to validate auto-rollback behavior
SLA validation: ensure 99th pct latency does not degrade beyond configured SLOs in canary runs
rollout_plan: Phase 0: internal-only experiments (Platform dev accounts) — 1 week
Phase 1: opt-in customers via feature flag — 2 weeks
Phase 2: conservative autopilot for low-risk models (e.g., quantization/batching only) — 4 weeks
Phase 3: widen autopilot coverage with stricter thresholds and human-approval bypass options — ongoing
monitoring_and_metrics: quality_eval_delta: absolute drop in pass-rate on golden prompt set
rollback_count: number of automatic rollbacks per week
time_to_revert: median seconds from trigger to completed rollback
false_positive_rate: percent of rollbacks where post-hoc analysis shows no customer impact
risks_and_mitigation: False positives triggering unnecessary rollbacks — mitigation: require corroborating signals (cost+quality) and progressive thresholds
Latency regressions during canary apply — mitigation: pre-warm kernels and rate-limit canary traffic
Audit/Compliance concerns for autopilot — mitigation: immutable audit events, customer opt-out flag, and mandatory approval for private deployments
Complex interactions with other optimizers (e.g., compiler-driven kernels) — mitigation: dependency tagging and compatibility matrix
